clue.text: Parking place with greenery -certain to give delight

parts.note: P is the standard map and road-sign abbreviation for parking
a lea is a meadow or grassy field in poetic usage
certain means sure

explanation.surface: A grassy parking area is guaranteed to please visitors.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: both name a feeling of happiness or enjoyment.

clue.text: Coppers settle the difficulty

parts.note: coppers are low-value coins, and p stands for pence
to settle, as a bird does on a branch, is to light or alight

explanation.surface: The police officers sort out the trouble.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Coppers' suggests police, but here it means copper coins, pennies, abbreviated P.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a plight is an unfortunate or troublesome situation.

clue.text: A country without conservationists yet perfect

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside, so the country's name surrounds the conservationists

parts.note: Eire is the Irish name for the Republic of Ireland
NT is the National Trust, the British heritage and conservation charity

explanation.surface: A nation lacking environmentalists is nevertheless flawless.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' reads as 'lacking', but here it has its old sense of outside, so the country's name surrounds the conservation charity.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: something whole and complete, with nothing missing, is perfect.

clue.text: Prompt with promises to pay-not genuine

parts.note: to prompt is to spur someone on
IOUs, written as I owe you, are promises to pay a debt

explanation.surface: Encouraged by pledges of payment that turn out to be fake.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: something spurious is false or fake, not what it claims to be.

clue.text: Concerned with the Spanish dance

parts.note: re means regarding or concerning, as in a letter heading
el is the Spanish word for the

explanation.surface: Something to do with the dance of Spain.
explanation.walkthrough: A REEL is a lively Scottish or Irish folk dance, not a Spanish one, which is the surface's trick.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a reel is a fast folk dance from Scotland and Ireland.

clue.text: Trains one right for added strength

parts.note: BR is British Rail, the former UK national railway
an ace counts as one in cards and dice

explanation.surface: Someone does training sessions to build up extra muscle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Trains' looks like a verb about exercise, but it is BR, British Rail.
explanation.definitionFit: A bracer is a stiff drink or tonic taken to fortify oneself, giving extra vigour.

clue.text: After one port Edward behaved most reprehensively

indicators.note: Edward is placed after the port, so these words fix the order of the two pieces

parts.note: Rio de Janeiro is a Brazilian port
Ted is a short form of the name Edward

explanation.surface: Having called at a harbour, Edward misbehaved badly.
explanation.definitionFit: To riot is to take part in a violent public disturbance, very bad conduct.

clue.text: Argues against ministers

parts.note: con means against, as in pros and cons
to minister to someone is to tend them, so ministers here is a verb

explanation.surface: Someone disputes the case against government ministers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ministers' reads as a noun for politicians but is the verb, as in ministering to the sick.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: to contend is to assert or maintain in argument.

clue.text: List the Conservatives as "circulating"

parts.note: a rota is a list of duties and who performs them
Tory is the familiar name for the British Conservative Party or a member of it

explanation.surface: A list describes the Conservative Party as moving around.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: rotatory means turning round, moving in a circle.

clue.text: Isn't rude maybe — but doesn't wait for an invitation!

indicators.note: maybe suggests the letters could be arranged another way

explanation.surface: Someone who is not impolite may still turn up uninvited.
explanation.definitionFit: To intrude is to enter where one is not welcome or invited.

clue.text: Issue catch lines

parts.note: issue means offspring, so a son
to net is to catch, as with fish

explanation.surface: A publication edition captures some verses.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Issue' suggests a magazine but means offspring; 'lines' is the poem.
explanation.definitionFit: A sonnet is a poem of fourteen lines, so lines of verse stand for it.

clue.text: Banner of a Quaker, a hard worker

parts.note: William Penn was the Quaker who founded Pennsylvania
the ant is proverbially industrious

explanation.surface: A flag belonging to a diligent member of the Society of Friends.
explanation.definitionFit: A pennant is a long tapering flag, a kind of banner.

clue.text: Within this His Eminence has to hold back

parts.note: HE abbreviates His Eminence, a cardinal's title
to rein in is to restrain or hold back

explanation.surface: Inside, the cardinal has to restrain himself.
explanation.definitionFit: Formal synonym: legal and literary English uses it for in this document or place.

clue.text: Dwelling with Oriental people in temporary shelter

indicators.note: the Oriental people are placed in the temporary shelter

parts.note: a tent is a portable, temporary shelter
E stands for East, so Oriental gives E
men are people

explanation.surface: A home where Eastern folk live under canvas.
explanation.definitionFit: A tenement is a large building divided into flats, so a residence.

clue.text: Performance of top man in the squeeze

indicators.note: the top man sits in the squeeze, so his letters go inside

parts.note: to press is to squeeze
OC is Officer Commanding, the man at the top of a unit

explanation.surface: The boss's act while caught in a tight crush.
explanation.walkthrough: 'top man' could suggest a boss or chief; the army abbreviation for Officer Commanding is what fits inside.
explanation.definitionFit: A process is the carrying out of a sequence of actions, the doing of a task.

clue.text: Charge after a dog, being up-to date

indicators.note: the charge comes after the dog, placing the second piece behind the first

parts.note: a cur is a mongrel dog
rent is a charge paid for property

explanation.surface: Running after a dog while staying fashionable.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: current means belonging to the present time, modern.

clue.text: A river in flood eroding its banks

indicators.note: in signals that the river lies within the words flood eroding

explanation.surface: A swollen river wears away at its banks.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters run across 'flOOD ERoding'; 'its banks' completes the picture of a river in spate.
explanation.definitionFit: The Oder is a central European river forming part of the German–Polish border.

clue.text: Lay out money to advantage?

explanation.surface: Is it beneficial to spend cash?
explanation.definitionFit: To spend money on something is to buy it; a purchase is also a firm grip or leverage, a mechanical advantage.

clue.text: The cabinet takes care — tell doubtful constituents

indicators.note: the components of the two words are uncertain, so their letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: The government's cabinet is careful, but its members are told they are unreliable.
explanation.walkthrough: 'doubtful constituents' rearranges CARE and TELL; 'cabinet' sounds like government but is furniture.
explanation.definitionFit: A cellaret is a cabinet or sideboard for storing wine bottles.

clue.text: A jumpy creature often to be seen on the beach

definitions.text: A jumpy creature often to be seen on the beach

parts.words: A jumpy creature often to be seen on the beach
parts.note: jumpy suggests nervousness, but the creature literally jumps and lives in the sand by the sea

explanation.definitionFit: A tiny crustacean that leaps about on sandy shores, also called a beach hopper.

clue.text: American newspaper leader that's followed

parts.note: US is short for United States, hence American
the editor leads a newspaper, abbreviated ED

explanation.surface: A US paper's chief whom others obey.
explanation.definitionFit: A method that is employed or adopted is one being followed in practice.

clue.text: Disgrace lads can get involved in

indicators.note: the letters become tangled up together, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: Shame that young men may be drawn into.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a scandal is something shameful bringing public disgrace.

clue.text: Read many a piece of writing about fruit

annotationWithheld.why: Clue held as 'Read many a piece of writing about fruit': D (many) + A + MS + ON gives the answer, but 'Read' has no job and no source gives the printed text.
annotationWithheld.clue: Read many a piece of writing about fruit

clue.text: Gave is ordered — make a face

indicators.note: ordered means put into a new arrangement, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone did as instructed and pulled a grimace.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ordered' rearranges GAVE IS; 'make a face' suggests grimacing, but face is just the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a visage is a person's face or expression, a literary word.

clue.text: Leave an area troubled by drought

explanation.surface: Abandon a region suffering from lack of rain.
explanation.definitionFit: To desert is to abandon; a desert is also an arid region with scarce rainfall.

clue.text: Organisation left to slip into chaos

parts.note: CO abbreviates company, a business organisation
a lapse is a slip or minor error

explanation.surface: A company abandoned to decline into disorder.
explanation.definitionFit: A collapse is a sudden breakdown or failure that brings disorder.

clue.text: Counsel a daughter against immorality

parts.note: D is the genealogical abbreviation for daughter
vice is immoral conduct

explanation.surface: Guiding one's daughter away from bad behaviour.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: counsel as a noun is guidance or recommendations offered.

clue.text: Soft drink that's not highly coloured

parts.note: p is piano, the musical direction for softly
ale is a kind of beer

explanation.surface: A soft drink that lacks bright colouring.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Soft drink' reads as one phrase but splits into P, the musical soft, and ALE.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: pale means light in shade, lacking intensity of colour.

clue.text: A whale turned the ship over

indicators.note: turned means turned round, so the whale is read backwards

parts.note: the orc is the killer whale or grampus
SS is steamship, the prefix of a ship's name

explanation.surface: A whale capsized the vessel.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: across means on or to the other side, as over does.

clue.text: Hammer the man about fifty and scoff

indicators.note: the man is placed about fifty, so his letters surround it

parts.note: a man is a male
L is the Roman numeral for fifty
to scoff is to eat greedily, so ate

explanation.surface: Beat up a fellow of around fifty and eat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'scoff' means mock, but in British slang it means eat greedily.
explanation.definitionFit: To malleate is to beat metal into shape with a hammer.

clue.text: Former brown shirt still surviving

parts.note: ex means former, as in ex-wife
tan is a light brown
a T-shirt gives the letter T

explanation.surface: An ex-member of the Nazi Brownshirts is still alive.
explanation.walkthrough: 'brown shirt' suggests the Nazi paramilitaries, but splits into TAN and T.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: extant means still in existence, not destroyed or lost.

clue.text: Rotten sales-pitch in fair

indicators.note: the sales pitch is placed in the word for fair

parts.note: decent means fair or reasonable
an ad is an advertisement, a sales pitch

explanation.surface: A dishonest patter at the funfair.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fair' suggests a funfair but means DECENT.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: decadent means morally decayed or degenerate.
